Jerome E. Brooks
134 West 92 Street
New York 25, N. Y.

Job Record and Qualifications

Research director of a project on the history of tobacco. Editor and author of the published text.

The project was underwritten by George Arents, a tobacco financier. His rare book collection formed the basis of the history. A large staff of researchers and translators worked under my direction in Europe and the United States. The material collected was published in four volumes between 1938 and 1943.

Vice President, Philip E. Wilcox, Inc., formerly at 39 Park Avenue. (Philip E. Wilcox, President.)

This firm specialized in the production of industrial and educational literature. Its publications were part of the personnel training, sales promotion, public relations, and product information programs of major business houses and associations. My work included client contact and counsel, sales presentations, and supervision of part of the writing staff.

Originally employed as editorial coordinator of a group of writers producing training manuals for the United States Navy. 1943 to 1947

Employed in the industrial and educational film field from 1947 to date.

As an account executive and writer with Caravel Films, Inc., 730 Fifth Avenue. (D. Pincus, Pres.)

As Sales Promotion Manager with Willard Pictures, 45 West 45 St. (John M. Squiers, General Manager.)

These jobs required a good deal of research in the fields of education and industry (as preliminaries to presentations and scripts), sales correspondence, and the development of film programs.
Additionally I have handled a number of special assignments as a sales promotion writer, and have created publicity for various projects. Author of The Mighty Leaf, a popular account of the tobacco industry.

Special skills are in the fields of writing, editing, and research.
